newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES' AUSSIE PITCHER HAS SUCCESSFUL SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES' AUSSIE PITCHER HAS SUCCESSFUL SURGERY.

text.p: The New York Yankees' Australian relief pitcher Graeme Lloyd underwent successful arthroscopic surgery Monday to remove a bone spur from his left elbow, the team announced Tuesday.

The surgery was performed by Doctors Stuart Hershon and Melvin Rosenwasser at the Columbia Presbyterian Medical Centre in New York. The two had discovered the condition when Lloyd was acquired August 23 in a four-player trade from the Milwaukee Brewers.
Lloyd's treatment by New York fans went from boos to cheers. In the post-season the tall left-hander was a solid contributor to a Yankee bullpen key to New York's World Series championship.
Lloyd, 29, went 0-2 with 10 runs allowed in his first five appearances with the Yankees, spanning 1 2/3 innings. He was booed mercilessly before taking more than two weeks off to rest his arm.
He came back to surrender one run over four innings in his next eight outings.

Lloyd excelled in the post-season, pitching 5 1/3 scoreless innings in eight relief appearances. In four World Series appearances against the defending champion Atlanta Braves, he went 2 2/3 innings without yielding a hit or a run, and struck out four without a walk.
His parents Noel and Pauline made the trip from their sheep farm in Geelong to see him play in the World Series.

In continuing repercussions from the original deal that brought Lloyd to New York, the Yankees acquired infielder Gabby Martinez Tuesday from the Brewers as the player to be named later in the Ricky Bones deal from August 29.
Bones was sent to New York as compensation for the injured status of infielder Pat Listach, who came over with Lloyd for outfielder Gerald Williams and pitcher Bob Wickman.
Yankee owner George Steinbrenner was critical of his own general manager, Bob Watson, for getting damaged goods -- Lloyd and Listach -- in the deal.
Lloyd had been 2-4 with no saves and a 2.82 ERA in 52 games with Milwaukee.
